title: Bounded coherent duality for a dualizing complex
statement: Let R be a commutative Noetherian ring, and let Omega belong to the derived category of R-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume Omega has a bounded representative of injective modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions], all its cohomology modules are finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and the scalar-action map R[0] -> RHom_R(Omega,Omega), transposed from the right unitor, is invertible. Then RHom_R(-,Omega) restricts to an anti-equivalence on the full subcategory of bounded complexes with finite cohomology [def-sf-coefficient-duality]. The restricted functor has a natural isomorphism, after inclusion into the ambient derived category, with the ambient internal Hom into Omega. No localness, completeness, Artinianity, or perfectness assumption is imposed on R or the input complexes.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, bounded clause; Definition 0A7B gives the three hypotheses.

proof.text: Use the exact equivalence between ordinary modules and modules on the one-object bottom-topology ringed site. The constant module functor and evaluation at its unique object are inverse: every restriction is an identity. They identify Hom and tensor products and preserve bounded complexes, injective terms, and finite cohomology. Their derived functors are inverse; uniqueness of tensor-Hom right adjoints identifies the existing ambient internal Hom and the ringed-site presentation in the cited lemmas. The component of the homothety is scalar multiplication, since it is the transpose of the right unitor.

Apply the finite-injective-dimension coherent RHom lemma to a coherent input K and Omega. It gives finite cohomology of D(K). If the chosen injective model I is supported in [a,b], good truncations represent K zero above c or below c; Hom into I is then zero below a-c or above b-c, respectively. These bounds show D exchanges bounded-below and bounded-above complexes, hence preserves bounded finite cohomology.

Each bounded-above good truncation of a finite-cohomology input is pseudo-coherent over the Noetherian ring. Apply the finite-injective evaluation lemma with L=M=Omega. The scalar-action isomorphism makes RHom(Omega,Omega) the tensor unit and supplies Tor amplitude [0,0]. Thus evaluation composed with scalar action and the inverse left unitor gives an invertible natural biduality map K -> D(D(K)). Its uncurrying is evaluation after Koszul interchange: scalar 1 acts as identity on Omega. Restrict D to the bounded finite subcategory. The natural bidual isomorphisms give its contravariant quasi-inverse; the ambient comparison is identity on objects and maps. The zero ring and empty cohomological support obey the same calculations.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, bounded clause; 0G4H for finiteness and More on Algebra 0A69 for canonical evaluation. Ordinary-module presentation and tensor-Hom identification spelled out by J1.

lean.statement:
theorem dualizingComplex_bounded_duality
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (Ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hI : ∃ I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ,
      (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero (I.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Injective (I.X i)) ∧ Nonempty (Q.obj I ≅ Ω))
    (hfinite : ∀ i : ℤ,
      Module.Finite R ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj Ω))
    (hscalar : IsIso (MonoidalClosed.curry (ρ_ Ω).hom)) :
    ∃ F : (WeilConjectures.boundedFiniteCoefficientComplex R).FullSubcategoryᵒᵖ ⥤
        (WeilConjectures.boundedFiniteCoefficientComplex R).FullSubcategory,
      F.IsEquivalence ∧
        Nonempty (F ⋙ (WeilConjectures.boundedFiniteCoefficientComplex R).ι ≅
          (WeilConjectures.boundedFiniteCoefficientComplex R).ι.op ⋙
            MonoidalClosed.internalHom.flip.obj Ω)
